library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Saqr_2025_mycophenolic_acid"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Saqr_2025_mycophenolic_acid"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3740>

Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) is converted to mycophenolic acid (MPA), which is
glucuronidated to the inactive MPAG and the minor acyl-glucuronide AcMPAG. MPAG
excreted in bile is deglucuronidated by bacterial beta-glucuronidases in the gut
and reabsorbed as MPA (enterohepatic circulation, EHC). Saqr 2025 fitted a
semi-mechanistic model in which the fraction of MPAG recirculated to MPA
(FrEHC) depends on the stool relative abundances of two bacterial communities:
community 1, dominated by *Bacteroides uniformis*, and community 2, dominated by
*Bacteroides vulgatus*.

# Population

Twenty adults (median age 46 years, IQR 36-55; median weight 87 kg, IQR 76-103;
40% female; 90% White, 10% American Indian) receiving hematopoietic cell
transplants for hematologic malignancies (Table 1). Post-transplant
immunosuppression was MMF 1000 mg IV every 8 h, infused over 2 h, plus
tacrolimus. Intensive sampling (0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 h after the start of
an infusion) took place on day 6-8 after transplant, after at least three
unchanged MMF doses (Supplementary File 1), and gave 480 plasma concentrations
of MPA, MPAG and AcMPAG. Stool for shotgun metagenomics was collected within
48 h of the PK sampling. Most patients were on antibiotics (levofloxacin 85%,
cefepime 55-70%).

The same information is available programmatically via
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Saqr_2025_mycophenolic_acid"))$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL_MPA) | 35.19 L/h/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (Vc_MPA) | 26.88 L/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `lcl_mpag` (CL_MPAG) | 3.69 L/h/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `lvc_mpag` (Vc_MPAG) | 18.83 L/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `lcl_acmpag` (CL_AcMPAG) | 73.78 L/h/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `lvc_acmpag` (Vc_AcMPAG) | 19.2 L/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `lq_acmpag` (Q_AcMPAG) | 37.11 L/h/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `lvp_acmpag` (Vp_AcMPAG) | 77.26 L/70 kg | Table 3 |
| `fm_mpag`, `fm_acmpag` | 0.87, 0.13 (fixed) | Supplementary File 3, Structural Model; Figure 1a |
| `logitfrehc` (FrEHC at median abundances) | logit(0.39) | Table 3; main-text Eq.1-4 |
| `lmtime1` (gallbladder emptying time) | 4.35 h | Table 3 |
| `dge` (emptying duration) | 0.5 h (fixed) | Supplementary File 3 (MTIME(2) = MTIME(1) + 30 min) |
| `lkehc` (gallbladder emptying rate KGG) | 3.71 1/h (fixed) | Table 3 'K45 [fixed]'; Figure 1 legend |
| `lkicv` (K51, gut MPAG to MPA) | 0.18 1/h | Table 3 |
| `e_stool_community_bacteroides_uniformis_pct_frehc` | 0.19 | Table 3 'Bacterial community 1' |
| `e_stool_community_bacteroides_vulgatus_pct_frehc` | 0.10 | Table 3 'Bacterial community 2' |
| `etalcl`, `etalcl_mpag` and covariance | CV 13.1%, 56.4%; correlation 0.536 | Table 3 |
| `etalvc_mpag` | CV 33.1% | Table 3 |
| `etalmtime1` | CV 173.6% | Table 3 |
| `etalogitfrehc` | CV 89.1% | Table 3 |
| `etalcl_acmpag` | CV 49.9% | Table 3 |
| `propSd`, `propSd_mpag`, `propSd_acmpag` | 25.4%, 10.8%, 22.2% | Table 3 |
| FrEHC equation `logit(FrEHC) = logit(theta) + eta + sum(theta_cov * log(abundance / median))` | -- | Main text Eq.1-4 |
| Community medians 19.97% and 13.23% | -- | Supplementary Table S4 |
| `kbm = FrEHC * kel_mpag / (1 - FrEHC)` (paper KEHC) | -- | Supplementary File 3 Eq.2 |
| 75% of the biliary flux to the gallbladder, 25% direct to the gut | -- | Supplementary File 3; Figure 1a |
| Allometry: exponents 0.75 (CL, Q), 1 (V), -0.25 (K51), reference 70 kg | -- | Supplementary File 3 Eq.3 |
| Proportional residual error | -- | Supplementary File 3 Eq.5 |

The IIV variances are `log(1 + CV^2)` from the Table 3 CVs (the tabled omega^2
are rounded to two decimals, and footnote d defines CV as
`sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`). The proportional residual SDs are the tabled CVs
(footnote e: CV = sqrt(sigma^2)).

# Shared simulation helpers

The model has three observed outputs, so observation rows name the MPA central
compartment and carry `dvid = 1`; rxode2 then returns `Cc`, `Cc_mpag` and
`Cc_acmpag` on every observation row.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Saqr_2025_mycophenolic_acid")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

med_c1 <- 19.97
med_c2 <- 13.23

make_events <- function(amt, tau, n_dose, obs_times, ids = 1L) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = amt, dur = 2, ii = tau, addl = n_dose - 1, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(obs_times, cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame()
  ev$dvid <- ifelse(ev$evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_)
  out <- lapply(ids, function(i) dplyr::mutate(ev, id = i))
  dplyr::bind_rows(out)
}

trap_auc <- function(time, conc) {
  sum(diff(time) * (head(conc, -1) + tail(conc, -1)) / 2)
}
```

# Gallbladder and EHC contribution at steady state (Table 5)

Table 5 compares the reference model with a version without a gallbladder (all
biliary MPAG drains continuously into the gut) and one without EHC, for a
typical 70 kg patient with median community abundances on 1000 mg every 8 h.
The no-gallbladder model is obtained by holding the emptying gate open for the
whole interval with a very fast emptying rate, so the gallbladder becomes a
pass-through; the no-EHC model sets FrEHC to essentially zero.

```{r table5}
ev_ss <- make_events(1000, 8, 10, seq(72, 80, by = 0.05)) |>
  mutate(
    WT = 70,
    STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT = med_c1,
    STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_VULGATUS_PCT = med_c2
  )

mod_no_gb <- rxode2::ini(mod_typ, lmtime1 = log(1e-8), dge = 1e6, lkehc = log(1000))
mod_no_ehc <- rxode2::ini(mod_typ, logitfrehc = -50)

ss_metrics <- function(m) {
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev_ss)) |> filter(time >= 72)
  c(auc = trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc), ctrough = s$Cc[s$time == 80])
}

tab5 <- rbind(
  "EHC with gallbladder (reference)" = ss_metrics(mod_typ),
  "EHC without gallbladder" = ss_metrics(mod_no_gb),
  "Without EHC and without gallbladder" = ss_metrics(mod_no_ehc)
)
tab5 <- data.frame(
  model = rownames(tab5),
  auc_sim = tab5[, "auc"],
  auc_pub = c(31.78, 31.85, 20.94),
  ctrough_sim = tab5[, "ctrough"],
  ctrough_pub = c(1.46, 1.34, 0.003),
  row.names = NULL
)
tab5 |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Model" = model,
    "AUC0-8 simulated (ug*h/mL)" = auc_sim,
    "AUC0-8 Table 5" = auc_pub,
    "Ctrough simulated (ug/mL)" = ctrough_sim,
    "Ctrough Table 5" = ctrough_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 5 of Saqr 2025 (typical-value medians; the paper's medians also integrate parameter uncertainty).")

# Typical-value solves of a linear model: a mis-transcribed clearance, volume,
# FrEHC or molar conversion moves these by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(tab5$auc_sim / tab5$auc_pub - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(tab5$ctrough_sim[1:2] / tab5$ctrough_pub[1:2] - 1) < 0.05),
  tab5$ctrough_sim[3] < 0.01
)
```

The steady-state AUC with EHC also has a closed form: with no EHC the MPA AUC
over a dosing interval is the MPA molar dose divided by CL_MPA, and EHC returns a
fraction 0.87 x FrEHC of every pass, so the AUC is inflated by
`1 / (1 - 0.87 * FrEHC)`:

```{r closed-form}
dose_mpa_mg <- 1000 / 433.49 * 320.34
auc_no_ehc <- dose_mpa_mg / 35.19
auc_ehc <- auc_no_ehc / (1 - 0.87 * 0.39)
c(no_ehc = auc_no_ehc, with_ehc = auc_ehc, ehc_share = 1 - auc_no_ehc / auc_ehc)
stopifnot(abs(tab5$auc_sim[1] / auc_ehc - 1) < 0.005)
```

The EHC share of the MPA AUC, `r round(100 * (1 - auc_no_ehc / auc_ehc))`%, is
the 34% reported in the Results.

# Microbiome community effects (Table 4)

Table 4 gives the change in FrEHC and in MPA, MPAG and AcMPAG AUC0-8 and trough
when one community abundance is moved to its observed minimum, 25th percentile,
75th percentile or maximum (Supplementary Table S4) with the other held at its
median. The tabled exposure changes are reproduced by the **first** 1000 mg dose
of a 2 h infusion with the 0-8 h window, not by steady state (the AUC changes at
steady state are several-fold larger, as Table 5 implies); the simulation below
therefore uses a single dose.

Zero abundances were replaced by one tenth of the smallest non-zero relative
abundance in the authors' dataset before log-transformation (Supplementary
File 5), a value the paper does not print. It is back-solved here from the
-80% (community 1) and -52% (community 2) FrEHC changes in Table 4.

```{r floor}
logit_ref <- qlogis(0.39)
floor_c1 <- med_c1 * exp((qlogis(0.39 * (1 - 0.80)) - logit_ref) / 0.19)
floor_c2 <- med_c2 * exp((qlogis(0.39 * (1 - 0.52)) - logit_ref) / 0.10)
zero_floor <- exp(mean(log(c(floor_c1, floor_c2))))
c(from_community1 = floor_c1, from_community2 = floor_c2, used = zero_floor)
```

```{r table4}
ev_sd <- make_events(1000, 8, 1, seq(0, 8, by = 0.05)) |> mutate(WT = 70)

first_dose_metrics <- function(c1, c2) {
  e <- ev_sd |>
    mutate(
      STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT = c1,
      STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_VULGATUS_PCT = c2
    )
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, e))
  c(
    FrEHC = s$frehc[1],
    `MPA AUC0-8` = trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc),
    `MPA trough` = s$Cc[s$time == 8],
    `MPAG AUC0-8` = trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc_mpag),
    `MPAG trough` = s$Cc_mpag[s$time == 8],
    `AcMPAG AUC0-8` = trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc_acmpag),
    `AcMPAG trough` = s$Cc_acmpag[s$time == 8]
  )
}
ref <- first_dose_metrics(med_c1, med_c2)

scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~community, ~abundance, ~c1, ~c2,
  "Community 1", "73.44 (max)", 73.44, med_c2,
  "Community 1", "36.75 (75th pct)", 36.75, med_c2,
  "Community 1", "3.63 (25th pct)", 3.63, med_c2,
  "Community 1", "0 (very low)", zero_floor, med_c2,
  "Community 2", "89.23 (max)", med_c1, 89.23,
  "Community 2", "41.76 (75th pct)", med_c1, 41.76,
  "Community 2", "0 (25th pct / very low)", med_c1, zero_floor
)

# Table 4 '% change from the reference' point estimates, in the scenario order
# above (columns FrEHC, MPA AUC, MPA trough, MPAG AUC, MPAG trough, AcMPAG AUC,
# AcMPAG trough).
pub4 <- rbind(
  c(15, 2, 21, -6, -10, 1, 11),
  c(7, 1, 10, -3, -5, 1, 5),
  c(-19, -2, -23, 7, 12, -1, -12),
  c(-80, -6, -83, 24, 48, -5, -42),
  c(12, 1, 16, -4, -8, 1, 8),
  c(7, 1, 10, -3, -4, 1, 5),
  c(-52, -4, -58, 16, 31, -3, -29)
)

sim4 <- t(mapply(function(a, b) 100 * (first_dose_metrics(a, b) / ref - 1), scen$c1, scen$c2))
colnames(pub4) <- colnames(sim4)

tab4 <- bind_cols(
  scen |> select(community, abundance),
  as.data.frame(sim4) |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ round(.x))),
) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(community, abundance), names_to = "metric", values_to = "simulated") |>
  mutate(published = as.vector(t(pub4)))

tab4 |>
  rename(
    "Community" = community,
    "Relative abundance (%)" = abundance,
    "Metric" = metric,
    "Simulated % change" = simulated,
    "Table 4 % change" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 4 of Saqr 2025 (first 1000 mg IV dose, 70 kg, other community at its median).")

# Deterministic typical-value solves. The published values are rounded
# medians over parameter uncertainty, so allow 3 percentage points.
stopifnot(max(abs(sim4 - pub4)) <= 3)
```

# Virtual cohort and NCA against the observed data

A stochastic cohort reproduces the study design: 1000 mg IV every 8 h over 2 h,
sampled over the fourth dosing interval (after three unchanged doses). Body
weight is log-normal with the Table 1 median and IQR. The community abundances
are drawn independently by interpolating the Supplementary Table S4 quantiles,
with the zero fractions the Results state (15% for community 1, 25% for
community 2); the paper does not give their joint distribution. Two hundred
subjects are simulated.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251106)
n_sub <- 200

# Piecewise-linear inverse CDF through the Table S4 quantiles; a fraction
# p_zero of subjects has 0% abundance, entered as the zero floor.
draw_abundance <- function(n, p_zero, q, floor_val) {
  u <- stats::runif(n)
  vals <- stats::approx(c(p_zero, q$p), c(0, q$x), xout = pmax(u, p_zero))$y
  ifelse(u <= p_zero, floor_val, pmax(vals, floor_val))
}

cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = exp(stats::rnorm(n_sub, log(87), log(103 / 76) / (2 * stats::qnorm(0.75)))),
  STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT = draw_abundance(
    n_sub, 0.15, list(p = c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1), x = c(3.63, 19.97, 36.75, 73.44)), zero_floor
  ),
  STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_VULGATUS_PCT = draw_abundance(
    n_sub, 0.25, list(p = c(0.50, 0.75, 1), x = c(13.23, 41.76, 89.23)), zero_floor
  )
)

obs_times <- 24 + c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5, 5.5, 6, 6.5, 7, 7.5, 8)
ev_cohort <- make_events(1000, 8, 4, obs_times, ids = cohort$id) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id")

sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_cohort)) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 24)
```

```{r cohort-plot, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  select(id, tad, MPA = Cc, MPAG = Cc_mpag, AcMPAG = Cc_acmpag) |>
  pivot_longer(c(MPA, MPAG, AcMPAG), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, c("MPA", "MPAG", "AcMPAG"))) |>
  group_by(analyte, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of the 4th infusion (h)", y = "Concentration (ug/mL)",
    title = "Simulated 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles",
    caption = "Compare with the observed profiles in Supplementary Figure S1 of Saqr 2025."
  )
```

PKNCA computes AUC0-8 for each analyte over the sampled interval. The reference
values are the medians of the per-patient AUC0-8 values in Supplementary Tables
S1-S3 (observed data, linear trapezoidal rule).

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim |>
  select(id, tad, MPA = Cc, MPAG = Cc_mpag, AcMPAG = Cc_acmpag) |>
  pivot_longer(c(MPA, MPAG, AcMPAG), names_to = "treatment", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc))
nca_dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, treatment = c("MPA", "MPAG", "AcMPAG")) |>
  mutate(tad = 0, amt = 1000)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ tad | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ tad | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals,
                   options = list(auc.method = "linear"))
)

obs_auc <- list(
  MPA = c(23.25, 19.39, 27.43, 14.15, 32.65, 18.04, 11.69, 23.23, 28.52, 28.47,
          22.42, 19.81, 8.07, 16.54, 19.32, 28.82, 12.75, 7.84, 18.20, 12.74),
  MPAG = c(204.97, 162.89, 311.08, 265.23, 295.98, 228.68, 127.30, 321.25, 182.73,
           418.47, 249.19, 193.61, 64.59, 163.00, 150.00, 210.41, 114.03, 212.29,
           340.60, 173.34),
  AcMPAG = c(1.856871, 2.85717, 4.683403, 2.255293, 8.119287, 3.707576, 0.744426,
             2.333183, 1.413583, 1.730086, 1.716368, 2.6533, 1.035319, 2.452901,
             2.733521, 1.258568, 0.837166, 1.214312, 3.149763, 1.146695)
)
published_nca <- data.frame(
  treatment = names(obs_auc),
  auclast = vapply(obs_auc, median, numeric(1))
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Median AUC0-8 over the 4th dosing interval: simulated cohort vs the observed NCA of Supplementary Tables S1-S3.")
```

```{r nca-gate}
sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(published_nca, by = "treatment")
sim_auc
# Centre of the distribution only: the extremes of a random cohort are not
# reproducible across rxode2 builds. A wrong clearance, volume or molar
# conversion moves the median by far more than 35%.
stopifnot(all(abs(sim_auc$sim / sim_auc$auclast - 1) < 0.35))
```

```{r table2}
mpa_auc24 <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", treatment == "MPA") |>
  mutate(auc24 = 3 * PPORRES)
tibble::tibble(
  class = c("Below (< 60)", "Within (60-120)", "Above (> 120)"),
  simulated_pct = round(100 * c(
    mean(mpa_auc24$auc24 < 60),
    mean(mpa_auc24$auc24 >= 60 & mpa_auc24$auc24 <= 120),
    mean(mpa_auc24$auc24 > 120)
  )),
  observed_pct = c(55, 45, 0)
) |>
  rename(
    "MPA AUC cumulative 24 h (ug*h/mL)" = class,
    "Simulated %" = simulated_pct,
    "Table 2 observed %" = observed_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Therapeutic-target classification of 3 x AUC0-8 (Table 2 of Saqr 2025).")
```

# Dosing regimens and community abundance (Figure 2)

Figure 2 simulated eight IV regimens (1000, 1250, 1500 and 1750 mg every 8 or
12 h, ten doses each) in a 1,000-subject copula-generated population and
reported the percentage with a cumulative 24-h MPA AUC in the 60-120 ug*h/mL
target, by community abundance group (low: up to the 10th percentile;
moderate: 10th-50th; high: above the 50th). The copula population is not
published, so the cohort here reuses the independent-draw abundances above with
200 subjects per regimen and groups subjects by their community 1 abundance
(Figure 2 panels a and b). Patients in the low group have essentially no EHC.

```{r fig2}
regimens <- tidyr::expand_grid(amt = c(1000, 1250, 1500, 1750), tau = c(8, 12)) |>
  mutate(regimen = paste0(amt, " mg Q", tau))

c1_q10 <- stats::quantile(cohort$STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT, 0.10)
c1_q50 <- stats::quantile(cohort$STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT, 0.50)
cohort_grp <- cohort |>
  mutate(group = case_when(
    STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT <= c1_q10 ~ "Low",
    STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT <= c1_q50 ~ "Moderate",
    TRUE ~ "High"
  ))

auc24_regimen <- function(amt, tau) {
  t_end <- 10 * tau
  ev <- make_events(amt, tau, 10, seq(t_end - 24, t_end, by = 0.25), ids = cohort_grp$id) |>
    left_join(cohort_grp, by = "id")
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, keep = "group"))
  s |>
    group_by(id, group) |>
    summarise(auc24 = trap_auc(time, Cc), .groups = "drop")
}

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251107)
fig2 <- regimens |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(res = list(auc24_regimen(amt, tau))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  tidyr::unnest(res) |>
  mutate(
    regimen = factor(regimen, unique(regimens$regimen)),
    group = factor(group, c("Low", "Moderate", "High"))
  )

fig2 |>
  ggplot(aes(group, auc24)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(60, 120), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, nrow = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Community 1 relative abundance group",
    y = "MPA AUC cumulative 24 h (ug*h/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 2a-b of Saqr 2025."
  )

fig2 |>
  group_by(regimen, group) |>
  summarise(pct_target = round(100 * mean(auc24 >= 60 & auc24 <= 120)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = pct_target) |>
  rename("Regimen" = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated % of subjects within the 60-120 ug*h/mL target by community 1 group. Figure 2a-b reports, for Low / Moderate / High: 1000 mg Q8 70 / 86.8 / 84.6; 1250 mg Q8 99 / 92.8 / 64.2; 1000 mg Q12 1 / 10.5 / 45.6; 1500 mg Q12 71 / 86.5 / 83.6.")
```

```{r fig2-gate}
fig2_med <- fig2 |>
  group_by(amt, tau, group) |>
  summarise(med = median(auc24), .groups = "drop")
# Structural trends on group medians: 1750 mg exposure exceeds 1000 mg in every
# group, and the high-abundance group exceeds the low group in every regimen
# (the low group has essentially no EHC).
wide_dose <- fig2_med |> filter(amt %in% c(1000, 1750)) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(tau, group), names_from = amt, values_from = med)
wide_grp <- fig2_med |> filter(group %in% c("Low", "High")) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(amt, tau), names_from = group, values_from = med)
stopifnot(
  all(wide_dose$`1750` > wide_dose$`1000`),
  all(wide_grp$High > wide_grp$Low)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate names.** The two community abundances are carried as
  `STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_UNIFORMIS_PCT` (community 1) and
  `STOOL_COMMUNITY_BACTEROIDES_VULGATUS_PCT` (community 2), in percent. Each is
  the summed relative abundance of the community's member species listed in
  Supplementary Figure S3, so it is only meaningful for those species sets.
* **Zero abundance.** The authors replaced 0% by one tenth of the smallest
  non-zero relative abundance in their dataset, which is not printed. The value
  used here, `r signif(zero_floor, 2)`%, is back-solved from the Table 4 FrEHC
  changes. The model itself takes the abundance as supplied; a value of exactly
  0 gives FrEHC = 0.
* **Molar bookkeeping.** The authors converted doses and concentrations to
  molar units without printing molecular weights. The model uses 433.49 (MMF),
  320.34 (MPA) and 496.46 g/mol (MPAG and AcMPAG). The Table 5 AUC without EHC
  (20.94 ug*h/mL) equals the MPA molar dose divided by CL_MPA, which confirms the
  conversion.
* **Gallbladder emptying timing.** The NONMEM MTIME gate is reproduced as a
  window from `mtime1` to `mtime1 + 0.5 h` after the start of each infusion
  (`tad()`), following the "time after dose" axis of Figure 1a. Because the
  emptying time carries a large IIV (CV 174%), some simulated subjects have an
  emptying time longer than the dosing interval; their gallbladder then never
  empties and the 75% stored fraction accumulates, which lowers their MPA
  exposure. The paper does not say how this case was handled.
* **Allometric scaling of rate constants.** Supplementary File 3 scales "rate
  constants" with exponent -0.25. It is applied to the estimated K51 (`kicv`);
  the gallbladder emptying rate KGG is a fixed literature value and is not
  scaled, and the emptying time is not scaled. At the 70 kg reference this has
  no effect.
* **Table 4 is a first-dose simulation.** The Table 4 percentage changes are
  reproduced to within 1-2 percentage points by a single 1000 mg dose and not at
  steady state, although Supplementary Figures S11-S13 are titled "at steady
  state". Table 5 is reproduced at steady state.
* **Virtual population.** Body weight and the two community abundances are
  drawn independently; the copula population of Figure 2 (which also used 26
  external microbiome profiles) is not available, so the Figure 2 percentages are
  only approximated.
* **FrEHC IIV scale.** The FrEHC random effect is added on the logit scale
  (Eq.3); its variance is back-computed from the tabled CV with the same
  log-normal formula the paper used to tabulate it.
